routes.reason: Source of ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.0 for the local double Tits system and its affine Weyl group. RG2.0 and its successors own the rational topology, valued roots and parahoric filtration, and this is the adapter the paper needs from them.
Source of RG2.1 for the Iwahori–Weyl group, the length function and the Bruhat order on W̃, with the planned item A1 named at the same stage, which PROTOCOL §16 allows a source route to do.
Source of RG2.3 for the parahoric subgroups, the standard pairs and the Iwahori decomposition the paper works with; A3 is named there as a planned item.
Source of RG2.4 for the Newton point, the θ-twisted conjugacy invariants and the σ-fixed-point comparisons over the residue field; A2, A5, A6 and A7 are named as planned items at that stage.

Source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.1 for the integral compactly supported Hecke functions, the convolution and the level comparisons, with ten planned items named there. SR.1 owns exactly that material, and the library item H1 already ties the carrier to Mathlib's CompactlySupportedContinuousMap.

Part II of the Tau Ceti RootSystems roadmap for dominant subtraction and Demazure reduction, reusing the id RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure that PAPER-HE-21, PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-ZHOU-26 and PAPER-ZHU-17 already propose, with the same title once the hyphen is restored (see the correction). The area grouptheory is a galaxy id and the brief is 261 words.

Part II of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups for Newton cocenters and invariant distributions, 52 items. The title reproduces the parent's atlas title 'Smooth representations of local groups' exactly, the area representations is a galaxy id, and the brief is 376 words. SR.1 plans test-function convolution but no layer states the Newton decomposition of the cocenter, the congruence-cocenter generators, Howe finiteness or the rigid-graph presentation, and the id appears in no other extraction.

notes: Accept, with two corrections in place. Structure: 123 items (100 missing, 16 planned, 7 library), every missing item routed exactly once, all stage ids exist, all planned layer ids exist, both Part II parents exist, both areas are galaxy ids, and check_paper.py passes. The planned items that appear inside source routes are the provision of PROTOCOL §16, not a defect. All seventeen declarations behind the seven library items resolve at the pins, from CompactlySupportedContinuousMap and the six Representation.Coinvariants declarations through Tau Ceti's three TitsSystem Bruhat-cell lemmas to the modular character, Haar uniqueness and nonempty_sections_of_finite_inverse_system. Coverage: every numbered theorem, proposition, lemma and corollary of the paper is carried into an item or a finding; the only numbered items not carried are Remarks 2, 14 and 19, which are bibliographic attributions. Locators: 52 of 57 name-and-page checks land exactly, and the five others are proofs on the page after the statement (Theorem 23 stated p.24, Theorem 3 stated p.12) or external citations my checker misread ('BT Proposition 5.2.12'). First correction: the provenance. The recorded source.sha256 cannot be reproduced, because the Cambridge PDF is stamped per download — two downloads seconds apart gave 45002919… and 90b506ca…, identical in length and differing only in the /ModDate and the bytes downstream of it — which is also why this file records a different hash in source.continuation for the same URL. I added a note saying so and naming the reproducible pin, comparisonVersion.sha256 for arXiv v3, which does reproduce exactly (605d7e9c…). Second correction: the Part II title wrote 'Cartan–Killing' with an en dash where the parent's atlas title, and the same route in PAPER-HE-21, PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-ZHOU-26 and PAPER-ZHU-17, spell it with a hyphen; the prefix must reproduce the parent title exactly, so it now does. One observation for the maintainer, in a file that is not this job's: PAPER-LE-LEHUNG-LEVIN-ETAL-23 routes to the same roadmap id under a different title, 'Root systems, Part II: dominance, affine orders and admissible pairs'. All thirteen findings are confirmed at their locators in the published text. The four substantial ones hold up: E1's (a) is false as justified, because the image of a θ-twisted class in Ω is the coset [w] + (1 − θ)Ω rather than a θ-orbit, and Ω = Z² with θ the swap shows the difference; E3 and E6 both turn on the coefficient ring, where the printed proofs use finite generation of a dual and a dimension count that a general commutative Z[1/p]-algebra does not support; and E5's pro-p subgroup gives no σ-descent, which needs Lang's theorem for a connected unipotent group. Nothing was rejected or deleted, and I add no finding.
